title: Koszul-normalized algebraic diagonal generator and scalar-extension compatibility
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, let $R\to B$ be flat of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and fix a surjection $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Use ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived coinduction $C^T_D=R\operatorname{Hom}_T(D,-)$ with its precomposition action [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. Put $L=\Omega^n_{P/R}[n]$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], $C=C_B^P(L)$, $A=B_1\otimes_R B_2$, and $C_1=C\otimes_{B,p_1}^{\mathbf L}A$, where $p_1(b)=b\otimes1$. Let $\delta:A\to B$ be multiplication. There is a specified isomorphism $\kappa_P:C_B^A(C_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}B[0]$ in $D(B)$, defined as follows. Set $T=P\otimes_R B_2$, let $q:T\to A$ be the quotient on the first factor, and set $e=\delta q:T\to B_2$, $x_i\mapsto\bar x_i$. Flat coinduction base change identifies $C_1$ with $C_A^T(\Omega^n_{T/B_2}[n])$. Compose coinduction for $T\xrightarrow q A\xrightarrow\delta B$, using its evaluation counits, and then use the ordered graph Koszul resolution of $e$, with equations $x_i-\bar x_i$, to obtain
$$\kappa_P:C_B^A(C_1)\simeq C_B^T(\Omega^n_{T/B_2}[n])\simeq B.$$
The last map sends the dual top graph wedge tensored with $dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_n$ to $1$, with the cohomological tensor signs. Let $\xi_P:B\to C_1$ in $D(A)$ be the coinduction adjunct of $\kappa_P^{-1}:B\to C_B^A(C_1)$. Multiplication by $\xi_P$ is an isomorphism $B\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,C_1)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

For every ring map $R\to R'$ with $R'$ Noetherian, put $P'=P\otimes_RR'$, $B'=B\otimes_RR'$, $A'=B'\otimes_{R'}B'$. The evaluation-counit coinduction base-change comparison $C\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\simeq C_{B'}^{P'}(\Omega^n_{P'/R'}[n])$ carries the derived pullback of $\xi_P$ along $A\to A'$ to $\xi_{P'}$. These equalities respect identity and successive base changes; no flatness of $R\to R'$ is required.

The construction also applies to $P$ localized at finitely many elements whose images in $B$ are units, using the localized graph Koszul resolution. It commutes with simultaneous localization $P\to P_h$, $B\to B_{\bar h}$, and with base localization. In a polynomial refinement $Q=P[t]\twoheadrightarrow B$, $t\mapsto\bar a$ for a lift $a\in P$, the coinduction-transitivity comparison $C_B^Q(\Omega^{n+1}_{Q/R}[n+1])\to C$ obtained by evaluating the additional relation $t-a$ against $d(t-a)$ carries $\xi_Q$ to $\xi_P$. Its normalization is $\operatorname{dual}(t-a)\otimes d(t-a)\mapsto1$, with the new differential last. It is independent of the lift $a$ in the derived category and compatible with scalar extension and ordered iterated refinements. These are assertions about the specified graph-evaluation maps, not about arbitrary choices of generators of a rank-one module. No proper morphism, globally chosen dualizing pair, or comparison with a proper-duality adjoint is an input.

source.place: Agent compatibility lemma: explicit graph-Koszul and evaluation-counit construction underlying Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian), Tags 0A70/0A71 (coinduction), and Tags 0BZI/0BZJ (top-differential normalization and polynomial refinement). Scalar-extension compatibility is an additional assertion proved by this construction, not a verbatim claim of these tags.

proof.text: Finite presentation implies finite type; hence $B$ is Noetherian by the finite-type algebra lemma. Apply polynomial-quotient perfectness to $R\to B$, so $B[0]$ admits a bounded finite-projective $P$-resolution $F$. The ordered differentials identify $\Omega^n_{P/R}$ with the free line on $dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_n$. Apply perfect coinduction exchange to $P\to B$ and $P\to T=P\otimes_R B_2$. Indeed $P$ is $R$-free, and $B$ is $R$-flat, so $B\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T=B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_2=A$. The comparison is therefore an isomorphism $\beta:C_1\simeq C_A^T(\Omega^n_{T/B_2}[n])$, characterized by extension of the evaluation counit. This also fixes the coprojection: the original $B$ is $B_1$, and the coefficients in $T$ are $B_2$.

source.place: Agent explicit graph construction refining Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian)

proof.text: Compose $C_B^A(\beta)$ with the coinduction transitivity isomorphism for $T\to A\to B$. The latter is the unique right-adjoint comparison whose counit is the composite of the two evaluation counits. For $e:T=B_2[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to B_2$, the ordered graph Koszul complex on $f_i=x_i-\bar x_i$ is a finite-free resolution of $B$. Apply $\tau_f$ with its coefficient line identified by $e_i\mapsto dx_i$. This gives precisely the specified $\kappa_P:C_B^A(C_1)\simeq B[0]$, including its $B$-action and its top-wedge normalization. No resolution of the possibly nonperfect diagonal module over $A$ was used.

source.place: Agent explicit graph construction refining Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian)

proof.text: Define $\xi_P$ as the adjunct of $\kappa_P^{-1}$. The scalar morphism determined by multiplication with this class is $\kappa_P^{-1}$ itself, after restriction along $\delta$. In a coinduction model a $B$-linear adjunct $u$ corresponds to $b\mapsto u(b)(1)$, with inverse $h\mapsto(b'\mapsto h(b'b))$. Hence the image of $b$ under the multiplication morphism is $b\kappa_P^{-1}(1)=\kappa_P^{-1}(b)$. This proves that it is an isomorphism, since $\kappa_P$ is one, and identifies exactly the asserted class rather than an unspecified generator.

source.place: Agent explicit graph construction refining Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian)

proof.text: For $R\to R'$ choose the same $F$. Since $P$ is $R$-flat and $B$ is $R$-flat, $F\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P'=B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'=B'[0]$. The perfect exchange lemma thus applies to $P\to B$ and $P\to P'$ without flatness of $R'$. It gives the stated counit-mate map $c:C\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\simeq C'$. Differential base change identifies its coefficient line with the ordered volume over $P'$. The same argument over $T$ gives $A\otimes_T^{\mathbf L}T'=A'$ and $B\otimes_T^{\mathbf L}T'=B'$: $A=B_1\otimes_RB_2$ and $B$ are flat over $B_2$. The graph augmentation base changes to the graph augmentation over $B'_2$. Finally $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'=B'$ since $A'=A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ and $B$ is $R$-flat. These verify every Tor-independence needed in pulling back the class.

proof.text: The exchange maps in step 4 are mates of scalar-extended evaluation counits. Paste these counits for $T\to A\to B$: taking an adjunct in two stages evaluates $h$ first at $1$ and then at $1$, just as the one-stage adjunct does. Thus the exchange square for coinduction transitivity commutes. The remaining graph trace square commutes by scalar naturality of $\tau_f$. Take adjuncts of the resulting equality for $\kappa_P^{-1}$: it says $(c\otimes1)\xi_P'=\xi_{P'}$, where $\xi_P'$ denotes extension along $A\to A'$. This proves compatibility of the specified classes even though no perfectness of $B$ over $A$ is assumed. Identity and successive comparisons agree because their exchange mates are the same pasted counit and their trace maps send the same ordered top wedge to $1$.

source.place: Agent explicit graph construction refining Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian)

proof.text: For localization of $P$ at $h$ mapping to a unit of $B$, localization is flat and $B\otimes_PP_h=B$. The localized finite-projective resolution still resolves $B$, by exactness of localization, so perfect exchange identifies the coinduction objects. Localize the graph complex at $h(x)$; its augmentation still resolves $B$ because $h(\bar x)$ is a unit. The trace comparison is exactly the localized $\tau_f$. For simultaneous $B\to B_{\bar h}$, localize both diagonal factors, so $A$ becomes $A_{h_1h_2}$ and $T$ becomes the corresponding localization at $h(x)$ and $h(\bar x)$ in the coefficient factor. All these maps are flat. Apply the same argument to those localizations, and to any finite list by composition. Differential localization identifies the coefficient lines; their ordered top evaluations are unchanged. Base localization is already covered by steps 4--5. Thus both the localized construction and every asserted localization compatibility use the specified maps.

source.place: Agent explicit graph construction refining Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian)

proof.text: For $Q=P[t]\to B$, $t\mapsto\bar a$, use coinduction transitivity through $Q\to P$, $t\mapsto a$. The one-relation Koszul evaluation against $d(t-a)$ gives an isomorphism $u_a:C_Q\simeq C_P$; this is the polynomial-refinement comparison with its orientation fixed by $\tau_{t-a}$. In the graph ring $T[t]$, write $f_i=x_i-\bar x_i$ and $z=t-\bar a$. Then $t-a(x)=z-(a(x)-a(\bar x))$. Polynomial subtraction, one variable at a time, writes $a(x)-a(\bar x)=\sum_i b_i(x)f_i$. Thus the graph tuples $(f,z)$ and $(f,t-a(x))$ differ by a triangular matrix with diagonal $1$. Moreover $dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_n\wedge d(t-a)=dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_n\wedge dt$, by the differential basis formula. Apply Koszul evaluation pasting to $S=T[t]$ with first tuple $(t-a(x))$, whose quotient is $T$, and second tuple $f$: the composite of the graph-ring form of $u_a$ with $\tau_f$ is $\tau_{(t-a(x),f)}$ under $t^{\rm Ch}_{1,n}$ on $V_{t-a}[1]\otimes V_f[n]$. The comparison $u_a$ writes its coefficient with the new differential last, as $V_f[n]\otimes V_{t-a}[1]$. By the symmetry identity $\sigma^{\rm Ch}[n+1]\,t^{\rm Ch}_{n,1}=(-1)^n t^{\rm Ch}_{1,n}\,\sigma^{\rm Ch}$ for the shifted lines, the block interchange matches $t^{\rm Ch}_{n,1}$ followed by the top exterior map of the cyclic permutation $(t-a,f)\mapsto(f,t-a)$, which is $(-1)^n$ on ordered generators. The matrix clause of the pasting lemma for that permutation, and then for the triangular change, identifies the trace with $\tau_{(f,z)}$ on $dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_n\wedge dt$, the normalization of $\kappa_Q$; the extra equation and differential stay last. Pasting the evaluation counits and taking adjuncts as in step 5 proves $(u_a\otimes1)\xi_Q=\xi_P$.

source.place: Agent explicit graph construction refining Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian)

proof.text: The ordered-volume trivialization identifies $C_P$ and $C_Q$ with their polynomial shriek models. Polynomial relative perfectness gives pseudo-coherence, finite $R$-Tor amplitude, and the scalar isomorphism $B\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_P,C_P)$. If $a'$ is another lift, step 7 proves that both $u_a$ and $u_{a'}$ carry $\xi_Q$ to $\xi_P$. Their ratio is therefore multiplication by some $b\in B$ on $C_P$. Acting on $\xi_P$ gives $b\xi_P=\xi_P$; under $\kappa_P$, this is $b=1$. Hence $u_a=u_{a'}$ in $D(B)$. The same reasoning shows uniqueness of any class-preserving isomorphism between two such models. Scalar extensions and localizations preserve the maps by steps 5--7 and the naturality of $\tau$. Ordered iterated refinements preserve the class at each step, and their composites agree by that uniqueness; the trace-pasting lemma fixes their tensor signs. For $n=0$ all graph complexes and volume lines are the unit in degree zero. For $B=0$ every comparison is the unique map of zero objects. No domain, smoothness, lci or properness hypothesis was introduced.
